claim.pdf_says: SAME AS data-name-1  (13.18.49.2 General format - BOTH 'SAME' and 'AS' carry their own underline; verified by cropping and 3x-enlarging the printed line at 300 dpi: two distinct underline rules, one under SAME, one under AS)
claim.why_it_matters: In the general-format notation an underlined word is a REQUIRED word (5.2.6.2) while a word that appears without underlining is an OPTIONAL word that may be written or omitted at the user's choice (5.2.6.3). Dropping the underline from AS makes the transcription say that 'SAME data-name-1' is legal COBOL and that AS is noise. It is not: AS is a required word of the SAME AS clause. The whole format is two words, so the lost marker is the entire syntactic content of the second word.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against the 300 dpi render of page 508 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v508/spec_p508.png, printed page number 478). ATTEMPTED REFUTATIONS, ALL FAILED: (1) 'the underline is present but reflowed / on an adjacent line' - no; the transcription of 13.18.49.2 is a single line, specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21474, verified byte-exact as '<u>SAME</u> AS data-name-1' with no other markup anywhere on the page and no compensating figure-notes block. (2) 'the apparent second rule is a rendering artifact or part of a glyph' - no; a scan of the crop for horizontal dark runs finds the underline row at y=915 containing exactly TWO long runs: x0=273 length 103 px (spanning S-A-M-E) and x0=401 length 40 px (spanning A-S), separated by a ~25 px unmarked gap, with NO run under 'data-name-1' (which begins near x=455). The gap and the independent lengths rule out one continuous rule and rule out a descender/serif artifact. At 4x magnification the two rules are plainly separate strokes with the same weight and the same baseline offset. (3) 'the markdown uses a different convention for AS' - no; the transcription elsewhere marks AS as a required word with the same markup: line 12929 '<u>FUNCTION-ID</u>. user-function-name-1 [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ]', line 13552 PROGRAM-ID prototype, line 18390 'IS <u>EXTERNAL</u> [ <u>AS</u> literal-1 ]'. The convention is established, so line 21474 is an isolated omission, not a house style. (4) 'the difference does not change meaning' - no; per 8.3.2.4.2 Required words ('Keywords. Within each format, such words are uppercase and underlined') and 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words ('uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format'), and per 5.2.2 / 5.2.3, the un-underlined transcription asserts that 'SAME data-name-1' is a legal writing of the clause. It is not. CONCLUSION: WHAT I SEE on the printed page is two distinct underline rules, one under SAME and one under AS, and data-name-1 unmarked. The finding is genuine and normative.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with one correction to the claim's citations. The substance is exactly right: the printed 13.18.49.2 General format underlines BOTH keywords - 'SAME' and 'AS' each carry their own separate rule (measured at 300 dpi: rules at x=273 len 103 and x=401 len 40 on scan row y=915, with a 25 px gap between them), while 'data-name-1' is unmarked. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21474 transcribes only '<u>SAME</u> AS data-name-1', losing the required-word marker on AS and thereby making the transcription assert that AS is an optional word and that 'SAME data-name-1' is legal COBOL. The fix is '<u>SAME</u> <u>AS</u> data-name-1'. CITATION CORRECTION: the claim attributes the required/optional-word notation to 5.2.6.2 and 5.2.6.3, but those subclauses are 'Brackets' and 'Braces'. The governing subclauses are 8.3.2.4.2 (Required words - keywords are uppercase and underlined) and 8.3.2.4.3 (Optional words - uppercase and not underlined, specifiable at the user's option), with the corresponding definitions at 5.2.2 (Keywords) and 5.2.3 (Optional words). The mis-citation does not affect the finding.
